# Voltage Drop Calculator: what size wire?

> Free voltage drop and wire size calculator. From the source voltage, the load (amps or watts) and the one-way run length it gives the voltage drop in volts and percent for every AWG, kcmil or mm² conductor, the smallest size within a target percentage, the longest run and the most current each size allows, the watts lost in the wire and, with hours and a price, the yearly cost of those losses. DC (12, 24, 48 V), single-phase and three-phase AC with power factor and optional reactance; copper or aluminium; solid or stranded; any conductor temperature; parallel sets. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Resistance is computed from conductor geometry and material constants (copper 100 % IACS, aluminium 61 % IACS, 2 % for stranding), not copied from a code table, and can be a few percent below published tables for some sizes; a value from the reader's own table can replace it. Ampacity is not checked: the reader enters the smallest size their ampacity table allows and the tool never recommends below it. Results are arithmetic on the numbers typed in, not electrical or code-compliance advice.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/voltage-drop-calculator/)
- [What size wire for 12 volts? 30 A over 15 ft, worked](https://marisstella.app/voltage-drop-calculator/what-size-wire-for-12-volts.html)

## For agents

- Engine: `calc.mjs`, `analyze(input)`; `DEFAULTS` is the page's example (30 A at 12 V DC, 15 ft). Callable through `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call voltage-drop-calculator analyze --input '{"system":"ac3","volts":480,"load":100,"length":300}'` or the repository's MCP server (`call_tool`).
